# Work-item traceability

Each board card has exactly one evidence record: `work-items/<card-id>.md`. The board stays authoritative
for state, priority, WIP, owners, and timestamps. The record holds what the board cannot hold: the shape
of the item, and the evidence of what happened to it. The rules are in `work-items/README.md`. This skill
is how to follow them.

## Create

- Create the record when the card is shaped or committed, whichever produces evidence first. Start from
  `work-items/TEMPLATE.md` and keep its section order.
- The file name is the card ID exactly, and it never changes. Never create a second record for the same
  card.
- Fill the identity block from the board and the brief. A field with no honest value is written as
  `unknown: <owner>, review by <date>` or `not yet; needed by <stage>`.

## Edit the description, append the log

- Sections above **Log** describe the item. Edit them as understanding improves. When an edit changes
  scope or acceptance criteria, add a log entry that says what changed and why.
- The **Log** is append-only, oldest first. Never edit or delete an earlier entry, including your own.

## Persist stage records

- Before a product candidate exists, the orchestrator commits the stage's declared artifacts and log entry
  on the card branch before dispatching the next stage.
- The implementer commits the product candidate first, obtains its full ID, and returns the candidate-change
  entry for the orchestrator to append. Reviewer, validation, and release agents also return their entries.
- The orchestrator commits each returned entry as an evidence-only commit. After a candidate exists, it may
  only append under `work-items/<card-id>.md`'s `## Log`; inspect the staged diff before committing.
- The candidate remains immutable and must be an ancestor of the branch head. If any other content changed
  after it, treat the latest product-changing commit as a new candidate and repeat review and validation.
- End every handoff with a clean working tree. Evidence commits are local and carry the same
  `Kanban: <card-id>` trailer; they are not new candidates.

## Log entry shape

```markdown
### YYYY-MM-DD: <event summary> (<stage or role>)

- Event: handoff | gate result: pass | gate result: fail | blocker raised | blocker cleared | rework to `<state>` | candidate change | release event | escalation to full | correction of the YYYY-MM-DD "<summary>" entry
- Candidate: `<full 40-character commit id>` | `<artifact>@<version>` | `not-yet-built`
- Checks run: `<command>` gave <observed result: exit status and the relevant output>
- Checks recommended but not run: `<command>`, because <reason>
- Evidence: <paths, test names, short excerpts, links>
- Next: <owner or stage>, <action>
```

- Get the date from the system (`date -u +%Y-%m-%d`). For a new candidate, obtain the ID immediately
  after its product commit with `git rev-parse HEAD`. For later stages, use the candidate from the
  verified handoff packet, not the evidence-commit HEAD. Never type a commit ID from memory.
- "Checks run" lists only commands run in this task, with the result actually observed. Quote the failing
  lines of a failure. Summarize a success, for example "exit 0; 142 tests passed, 0 failed".
- One entry per material event. Every stage handoff and every gate result is material.

## Blockers (K §4.4, §30.6)

A blocked card stays in its state and still counts against WIP. When you raise a blocker, add these lines
to the entry:

```markdown
- Blocked since: <timestamp>
- Condition: <what prevents progress>
- Impact on delivery: <what slips, and against which SLE>
- Unblock action and owner: <action> — <person or role>
- Next escalation: <when, and to whom>
- External dependency or contact: <if any>
```

Clear it with a `blocker cleared` entry that names how it was resolved.

## Rework

A rework entry names the target state and the finding IDs, and quotes each finding. The next stage reads
it as its input. Rework is a backward transition, not a state (K §4). The log is how rework frequency
stays visible.

## Corrections

When an earlier entry is wrong, append a `correction of the <date> "<summary>" entry` event. State what
was wrong, what is true, and the evidence. The wrong entry stays as it is.

## Decisions

Consequential decisions go into ADRs, never only into the log. Link each ADR from the "Decisions and ADRs"
table, with its current status.

## Confidentiality

Records are committed with the code. Keep secrets, credentials, personal data, customer data, and exploit
details out of them (K §22.3, §22.4). For a restricted security item, write "details in <restricted
location>" and record the location only.
